claim: OVERSHOOT-TARGET (medical-twin intervention half): the twin must IMPROVE ON the strongest available control at CHOOSING an intervention -- not predicting an outcome afterwards -- on a patient it has never seen, in a procedure it was not built for, with the instrument actually in the room, while the adversary is INFLATED beyond the real case: anatomy variation beyond the cohort, instrument error beyond specification, surgeon preference beyond protocol, and a target refraction that is not emmetropia. The strongest control is whatever practice actually uses, never a weakened one. A perpetual, non-converging frontier: each child that holds raises the inflation rather than closing the goal. Mirror of the cancer-immune goal overshoot, pointed at the intervention instead of the adversary. Today's standing is the floor, not the target: implant power closer to the hindsight correct value in 11 of 20 cases against 2, and residual astigmatism 0.282 D against practice's 0.626 D on 69 patients. Every folded child is a HYPOTHESIS until certified against a facit this project did not produce.
regime_note: preoperative biometry frozen postoperatively; mean-curvature scalar cornea for the power decision, three-meridian power vector for the toric decision; modelled lens design, not the implanted serial-number lens. Not a clinical recommendation.
draft_note: Draft node per the shared routine agreed with the dental lane 2026-10-03: new nodes go in an expansion file and are read next to the source graph, never written into it. A goal with an empty depends_on is a leaf, not a root: that is precisely why the source graph has one goal that nothing reaches, and my first draft reproduced it. depends_on points at prerequisites, so the goal depends on the decisions that achieve it.
unlocks: If it holds under inflation: the twin can be asked which intervention to perform before the intervention exists in any cohort, which is the only form in which a twin is worth more than a lookup table.
outclass: Strongest eligible control per decision, named explicitly: for power, the lens the surgeon actually implanted; for cylinder, the population-estimate posterior cornea that calculators use. Never a control weakened to make the win visible.

claim: Inverting the assembled chain turns it from a predictor into a chooser: the predicted refraction is monotone in implant power, so bisection yields the power that hits a target. Scored against the hindsight-correct power derived from each patient's MEASURED refraction, not against our own model -- the first version scored the twin against its own prediction, gave an impossible 20 of 20 inside tolerance, and is withdrawn. Bias removed leave-one-out so a patient never sees its own outcome; without that correction the mean miss is 0.678 D, so the correction does not carry the result.
regime_note: 20 spherical-IOL patients, target emmetropia, 0.5 D manufacturing grid.
unlocks: Unlocks every OTHER inverse question on the same chain: target refraction other than emmetropia, monovision, and the choice between two lenses that differ in more than power. The inversion is the reusable part, not the lens.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.

claim: The toric decision has three parts -- power, cylinder and axis -- and its value lies in a quantity practice does not measure. Standard calculators ESTIMATE posterior corneal astigmatism from a population regression; this cohort measures it. Using the measurement cuts residual-cylinder error from 0.626 D to 0.282 D against measured refraction. Three construction errors were found and fixed by implausible magnitudes: an unverified vergence chain giving 5.2 D residual, a lens cylinder that added to the cornea instead of cancelling it, and two-meridian sampling that cannot represent an oblique axis.
regime_note: 69 toric patients; incision-induced astigmatism, lens rotation and postoperative geometry change are NOT modelled.
unlocks: Unlocks the whole class of decisions where practice uses a POPULATION ESTIMATE for something this cohort measures. Once the pattern is established, every estimated-versus-measured pair in the model becomes a candidate decision with its own external control.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.

claim: An unbroken chain from molecular charge inventory to refractive power: halving the charge inventory lowers ionic swelling pressure by 489.65 Pa, pupil-mean thickness by 3.54 um and refractive power by 0.4256 D, with the Strehl ratio falling 0.1227 to 0.1042. A rotationally symmetric cornea of the same mean thickness gives 1.36e-08 D, so the entire effect comes from non-symmetric structure. Numerics clean to 4.19e-13 D. The SIGN is not yet determined: across twelve conditions the change spans +0.4658 D to -0.8618 D.
regime_note: clinical comparison against 20 held-out patients: 7 of 20 within 0.25 D, bias -0.3865 D thin lens against +0.1455 D thick.
unlocks: Unlocks asking what a molecular-level change does to vision, which is the only path from a drug or a hydration state to a clinical endpoint. Without it, molecular work cannot reach an outcome a patient would notice.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.

claim: The binding quantity for the DIRECTION of a corneal procedure's effect, and unlike the night's other missing measurements it is routinely acquired by a topographer. Thickness, index field, hydration AND surface allocation together leave 0.3056 D undetermined at identity errors exactly 0.0, in 4 of 4 pairs. With native pupil-limited shape data the maximum gap falls to 0.2396 D, below the 0.25 D clinical threshold, with 0 violations in 101 cases -- but at large pupil it is violated in 98 of 98. So the twin is determinate for photopic vision and indeterminate for mesopic, which is the clinical pattern of night-vision complaints.
regime_note: 102 native topography files acquired; pupil diameter is a regime axis, not a fixed value.
unlocks: Unlocks the DIRECTION of a procedure's effect, not only its magnitude, and it is the one missing quantity that is routinely acquired. It also unlocks the regime split: determinate for photopic vision, indeterminate for mesopic, which is a clinically recognised pattern we could not previously state.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.

claim: The lens was the dominant error term in the chain and is no longer: bias -0.3865 D with a thin lens against +0.1455 D with a thick one, and an index-convention control reproducing the thick-lens figure rules out a unit artefact. Resolved, the conditional power error is 0.0178 D at 1.0 um and 0.1 mrad tolerances, with an unavoidable per-state error of 0.0322 D against a 0.25 D clinical threshold. 36864 ray-state checks and 5120 interval checks with zero violations; 0 of 72 and 0 of 54 minimax witnesses found. Coarsest sufficient discretisation 16384 cells.
regime_note: raw device data acquired is a one-side strip of a different lens than the implanted one; the lane flags this itself.
unlocks: Unlocks attributing the remaining error to something other than the lens, which was impossible while the lens carried the dominant bias. It also unlocks the glass chain in the platform graph, which asks for exactly a lens judged by a raytrace cell -- this lane IS that judge.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.

claim: The quantity whose measurement beats practice's estimate. Measured against estimated differs by 0.5924 D on average in corneal cylinder across 69 patients, and carrying the measurement through the chain is better in 50 of 69 against 19. This is an information-link claim in its strict form: the control is current practice WITHOUT the new information, not an equally informed method.
regime_note: tomographer-measured anterior and posterior radii with axes; population estimate taken as 0.30 D against-the-rule at 90 degrees.
unlocks: Unlocks the comparison form itself: a control that is current practice WITHOUT the new information, rather than an equally informed method. Every quantity we measure and practice estimates can be tested this way.
outclass: Improve on the strongest eligible control for this node, named in the claim; a node that only beats a weaker control is not folded.
